newsitem.title: philippines: Philippine peso ends down on lower premium vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down on lower premium vs dlr.

text.p: The Philippine peso fell to 26.367 at the close on Wednesday from 26.355 as abritrage money left due its narrower interest premium, traders said.
A 0.25 percentage-point hike in the U.S. dollar rate and the Central Bank's cut in overnight borrowing rate to 9.9 from 10 percent led to the weakening of the peso, they said.
The day's average was at 26.367 from 26.351. Volume was lower at $305.4 million from $314.9 million.
As expected, the Central Bank came in to curb the peso's fall. It sold about $150 million at 26.37 pesos, traders said.
"The Central Bank coming in at 26.37 helped settle the market," a foreign bank trader said.
On Monday, the peso is expected to move sideways between 26.355 to 26.37 since the Central Bank is expected to cap the peso's movement, traders said.
"It would be safe to assume we've reached the peak for the dollar," the foreign bank dealer said. "I've seen some banks selling dollars."
